---
title: Near-Real-Time Processing
execute:
  eval: false
---

Poll a directory spool, process newly indexed patches, and stop after two empty polls. Choose the polling interval for the data cadence and storage latency.

```{python}
import time
from pathlib import Path

import dascore as dc
from dascore.units import s

input_dir = Path("/path/to/incoming/data")
output_dir = Path("/path/to/results")
output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

root = dc.spool(input_dir)
window = step = 10 * s
poll_seconds = 30
processed = 0
empty_polls = 0

while empty_polls < 2:
    root = root.update()
    spool = root.sort("time")
    new = spool[processed:]

    if len(new) == 0:
        empty_polls += 1
        time.sleep(poll_seconds)
        continue

    empty_polls = 0
    for offset, patch in enumerate(new):
        result = patch.rolling(time=window, step=step, engine="numpy").mean()
        name = f"processed_{processed + offset:06d}.h5"
        result.io.write(output_dir / name, "dasdae")

    processed = len(spool)
    time.sleep(poll_seconds)
```

For a long-running service, replace the two-poll exit with monitoring, retries, and a durable record of processed source IDs.
